item.title: Individual Project
item.description: Individual Project # This is your own project, separate from the team project. Use one individual GitHub Pages website throughout the semester and register its link in ML Class Hub. Update the same website at midterm and final; do not create a new link for each checkpoint. The course-specific Hub assignment will identify the required dataset, label mappings, and submission details once staff configure it. CIFAR-10 is an example, not a required dataset.

item.title: Categories
item.description: Grading Categories # The required course components total 100%. There is no final exam or optional project bonus. Component Course weight Quizzes 1–14 15% Midterm exam 15% Individual project 30% Team project 40% Total 100% Quiz 0 is required preparation but carries no course-grade weight. See Quizzes and Exams for assessment rules and Project Breakdown for the two project tracks. The project rubrics will describe how each stage is evaluated; this table does not assign separate course-grade percentages to project stages.

item.title: Collection
item.description: GT Resources # For any resources related to Student Engagement and Wellbeing such as Dean of Student’s contacts, Library, etc., please refer to this LINK Class Resources # Required Course Materials # No textbook will be required for this course, however you are strongly encouraged to complete the readings indicated for each class. You may also find the following books very helpful: Learning from data, by Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa Pattern recognition and machine learning, by Christopher Bishop Machine learning, by Tom Mitchell Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, by Jiawei Han, Micheline Kamber, and Jian Pei The Elements of Statistical Learning, by Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, and Jerome Friedman Deep Learning, by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville Other resources, such as machine learning toolboxes and datasets, will be provided throughout the course.

item.title: Course Overview
item.description: Course Overview # Important CSE students should note that CS 7641 is not allowed as a substitute for the CSE core course CSE 6740, and that they cannot get credit for both CSE 6740 and CS 7641. Course Description # This course introduces techniques in machine learning with an emphasis on algorithms and their applications to real-world data. We will investigate the following question: how to computationally extract useful knowledge from data for decision making and task support!

item.title: General
item.description: General Course Policies # Online participation and course materials # Core lectures are pre-recorded; live lecture attendance is not required. Study the assigned videos and notes, complete assessments within their availability windows, and work on both the individual and team projects. The schedule also links interactive visualizations and demonstrations when available. Course-created videos, notes, assessment questions, and code are for enrolled students. Do not redistribute them outside the course without written permission.

item.title: Team Proposal
item.description: Team Project Proposal # Submit a concise proposal on your team’s existing project website and register the website link and team in ML Class Hub by the date on the course schedule. Keep using this site through midterm and final; no separate proposal website is needed. This milestone is for the team project, not the individual project. Choose the question # Start with a real problem that your team can investigate within one semester.

item.title: Office Hours
item.description: Online Office Hours # Office hours are optional online help sessions. They do not replace scheduled project reviews. Joining a session # A TA announces the session in an Ed thread with the time and any focus topic. Reply with a short, specific question and what you have tried. Do not post private information, complete code, grades, or confidential project data. The TA answers in the thread when useful to the class, or sends a private meeting link when screen sharing or individual discussion is needed.

item.title: Team Midterm Review
item.description: Team Midterm Website Review and TA Meeting # Update the same team project website before your scheduled TA meeting. The meeting is the team midterm checkpoint. There is no separate team midterm report or video, and the individual project’s video is a different requirement. The course schedule gives the two-week review window; arrange the meeting with your assigned TA through the course process. Show progress, not a finished paper # On the website, state the current question and any change since the proposal; data access and preparation; a working baseline or early experiment if available; evaluation completed so far; honest failures and blockers; each member’s contribution; and the next concrete experiments.

item.title: Team Final Report
item.description: Team Final Report, Website, and TA Interview # The team delivers a paper-style report on the same team website, supporting code and reproduction instructions, and a TA interview. The interview is in the two-week final-review window; the completed website is due on the last instructional day shown in the course schedule. Keep the same ML Class Hub team link. The individual project’s final website and interview are separate; see Individual Project.

item.title: Awards and Examples
item.description: Project Awards and Examples # These awards recognize exceptional individual and team projects. They are distinct from course grades: an award is not needed for full credit, and the current Spring 2027 grading plan does not include extra course-grade points for awards. Every completed project is eligible for consideration; no separate award application is required. The final website and interview are the evidence reviewed. See Grading Categories for the course-grade weights.
